add.text: Current smoker
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 2 ('Aged over 55 years’ old, current smoker'). Current smoking only; ex-smoking is a different concept (footnote *2 'Current or past smoker' is not encoded).

add.text: Unexplained, new, or worsening dyspnoea
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list.

add.text: Unexplained cough, persisting and worsening for more than 3 weeks
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list.

add.text: Unexplained chest and/or shoulder pain persisting for more than 3 weeks
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list. X-ray Chest p62 prints this item without 'persisting for more than 3 weeks' - a different concept there.

add.text: Unexplained changes in existing symptoms in patients with underlying chronic respiratory problems persisting for more than 3 weeks
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list.

add.text: Unexplained hoarseness persisting for more than 3 weeks
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list.

add.text: Repeated / or unresolved chest infections
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list.

add.text: Persistent, unexplained haemoptysis
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list. Distinct from redflag.haemoptysisPresent (haemoptysis of any kind), which it implies.

add.text: Unexplained weight loss and loss of appetite persisting for more than 3 weeks
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list. Not weightloss.present: this item also requires loss of appetite and a duration of more than 3 weeks.

add.text: Un-investigated/unexplained abnormal chest signs persisting for more than 3 weeks. (e.g. suspected pleural effusion)
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list.

add.text: New, supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list.

add.text: Features suggestive of paraneoplastic syndromes. e.g. hypercalcaemia, hypertrophic osteoarthropathy with finger (and toe) clubbing and painful swollen joints
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list.

add.text: New cervical lymphadenopathy persisting for more than 3 weeks and nodes are more than 1 cm in diameter in a patient with other lung cancer symptoms or signs or risk factors
add.notes: Footnote *1 item on p15 ("Concerning symptoms and signs for lung cancer"). Text is the item as printed; the item's own duration / size qualifiers are part of the concept (CT Chest REVIEW Q4). X-ray Chest - Adult p62-63 prints a near-identical list. 'risk factors' refers to footnote *2, which is judged within this indicator rather than encoded separately.

add.text: The concerning symptoms or signs are of new onset
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 2 sub-bullet 1 ('One or more concerning, new onset, symptoms /signs for lung cancer'). Applies to the presenting symptoms/signs.

add.text: Symptoms or signs persistent for six weeks despite appropriate treatment
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 2 sub-bullet 2. 'for six weeks' read as at least six weeks (CT Chest REVIEW Q3).

add.text: Haemoptysis occurred in the absence of chest infection
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 1 parenthetical, first half (CT Chest REVIEW Q5).

add.text: Persistent, non-specific, non-localising symptoms and signs which are concerning for underlying cancer

attestationWording.referrer: Does the patient have persistent, non-specific, non-localising symptoms and signs that you are concerned are due to an underlying cancer?
attestationWording.triager: Does the referral describe persistent, non-specific, non-localising symptoms and signs concerning for underlying cancer?

add.notes: CT Chest alternative-management bullet 2 (redirect to the CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis HealthPathway). Proposed for the AD-17 attestation category: 'concerning for underlying cancer' is the referrer's clinical impression (CT Chest REVIEW Q14). '(e.g. weight loss, fatigue)' is illustrative and not part of the text.

add.text: Upper respiratory tract causes, including bleeding from the nasopharynx, sinuses or oral cavity, have been excluded
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 1 parenthetical, second half (CT Chest REVIEW Q5).

add.text: Initial investigations fail to identify a cause
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 1 ('initial investigations including chest x-ray fail to identify a cause'), P2 bullet 2 ('unexplained despite initial investigations including chest x-ray and blood tests') and alternative-management bullet 2 (p15). Which investigations were done is recorded by workup.cxr / workup.bloods.

add.text: Chest x-ray is normal
add.notes: CT Chest alternative-management bullet 1.

add.text: Indeterminate abnormality on chest x-ray which raises the possibility of a lung cancer (e.g. bulky hilum)
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 3. '(e.g. bulky hilum)' is illustrative (KI-05). See CT Chest REVIEW Q7 on isolated nodules.

add.text: Persistent consolidation on chest x-ray done as a 6-week follow-up study
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 4.

add.text: Isolated pulmonary nodule identified on a chest x-ray
add.notes: CT Chest P3 bullet 1. Printed 'Isolated, pulmonary nodule'.

add.text: The nodule cannot be confirmed as benign from x-ray appearances alone
add.notes: CT Chest P3 bullet 1.

add.text: The radiology report recommends the requested imaging
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullets 3 and 4 ('CT chest is recommended in the Radiology report') and P3 bullet 1 ('referral for CT chest is recommended in the Radiology report'). Worded for the requested exam, like advice.urgentImagingRecommended, so other sites can reuse it (CT Chest REVIEW Q6).

add.text: Patient re-presents with the symptoms or signs being referred (this is not the initial presentation)
add.notes: CT Chest alternative-management bullet 1 ('Patient re-presents'). Bullet 3's 'Initial presentation' is the same concept negated, but bullet 3 is not evaluated (CT Chest REVIEW Q8).

add.text: The request is for follow-up of a nodule discovered incidentally on a CT chest scan
add.notes: CT Chest alternative-management bullet 4.

add.text: The radiology report confirms the nodule is benign based on CT appearance and no follow-up is required
add.notes: CT Chest alternative-management bullet 4 ('unless radiology report confirms benign ...'). Examples printed: intrapulmonary lymph node, benign pattern of calcification (illustrative, KI-05).

add.text: A secondary care clinician or radiologist advises referral for urgent staging CT chest/liver for work up of a suspicious lesion on chest x-ray
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 5. Not advice.urgentImagingRecommended: the bullet names staging CT chest/liver and omits PCRL.

add.text: CT is the advised next step on the local HealthPathway, as opposed to referral to secondary care or PET-CT
add.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 5 (with footnote *4 'Local pathways–direct to PET CT', p16). Answered by the referrer for their district; the criterion itself is national.
